answer: Anchor every identity to one hardware enclave: on signup the device produces an attestation quote, a pigment mark burned into its secure chip that no software copy can reproduce. The network verifies the quote and nails the identity to that timber — one chip, one identity, and a quote reused across two accounts is rejected outright. An honest agent pays nothing beyond the device it already owns. A farmer wanting 1,000 fakes must buy 1,000 chips at $40 each, $40,000 before earning a cent. Only hardware-anchored identities climb to the summit tier of jobs.
